content:
Before approving a bill of lading draft for a Maersk shipment from China to the United States, ask your forwarder for the legal name of the Price Owner, the company whose rate arrangement is used with Maersk. Then ask which field on the carrier draft will show that company. Maersk’s November 25 advisory for trades regulated by the US Federal Maritime Commission (FMC) says the Price Owner must appear as the shipper, consignee or notify party. If you’re shipping less than a container load (LCL), ask who checks the carrier bill and who checks the house bill for your shipment.

  • Confirm whose rate was used. The forwarder who sends the quote may be booking as an agent.
  • For LCL, mark the carrier bill and house bill separately before checking the names.
  • Ask for the shipping-instruction deadline, the draft approver and the person who will request corrections.

What Maersk is asking booking parties to check

Maersk describes the Price Owner as its contractual customer. If an agent is acting for that company, the November 25 advisory says the agent’s name should appear in the shipper or consignee address with “On Behalf Of” or “As agents of” wording. Ask the booking party to confirm the exact name, field and wording for the booking before submitting the shipping instructions. Maersk says missing information can delay release of the final bill. The notice concerns Maersk documentation on FMC-regulated trades. It gives no revised sailing schedule.

Suppose your Ningbo supplier packs the goods, your US company buys them, and a forwarder emails the quote. The forwarder could be using its own rate as an NVOCC or booking as an agent for another company. Ask, “Whose rate is on the carrier booking, and where will that company appear on the draft?” Use the booking party’s answer to check the draft against the shipping instructions.

For LCL, check which draft is in front of you

In a consolidation, the vessel carrier’s master bill (MBL) and the non-vessel-operating common carrier’s house bill (HBL) can show different parties. The house bill covers your consignment. If the consolidator sends you an HBL draft showing your supplier and your US consignee, check those entries with the consolidator. Separately, ask the party who placed the Maersk booking to confirm that the Price Owner and any agency wording are recorded correctly on the carrier side.

If your contact can share only the HBL, ask for written confirmation that someone has checked the carrier draft and cleared any outstanding correction. For updates on what is holding up the paperwork, ask which document is pending and who needs to act. That lets you follow up with the document issuer while giving your US broker the correct reference for your shipment.

Bill of lading draft checklist

Field or checkpointWhat to ask the forwarderWho should confirm
Document and booking referenceIs this the carrier MBL or our HBL? Which booking and draft version are we checking?Forwarder or consolidator
Price Owner and agent wordingWhat is the legal name on the rate arrangement? Which Maersk documentation field carries it? If an agent acts for that company, what wording belongs in the shipper or consignee address?Party placing the Maersk booking
ShipperWhat exact legal name and address belong in the shipper field on this bill?Export contact and document issuer
Consignee and notify partyWho is named as consignee on this bill, and who should receive the notice? Verify the contact information with the receiving team.US receiving contact and document issuer
Cutoff and correctionWhen are shipping instructions due? Who checks the latest draft and requests a correction if a name or address is wrong?Forwarder’s documentation team

What to send when a draft is held up

Put the booking or HBL reference in the email subject. Mark the specific field on the latest draft and write the corrected name and address in the message. Ask whether the correction belongs on the house bill, carrier bill or both. Request a revised draft and agree when you’ll check back. If the final bill has already been issued, ask its issuer for the amendment process and any applicable charge.

Ask DDNZ about your China–US shipment. Send the origin, US destination, LCL or full-container shipment type, and booking stage. If you already have a draft, share a redacted copy showing the field you need to check.
